Package org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr

Class DataLoader

java.lang.Object
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.DataLoader
All Implemented Interfaces:
Iterable<Datum>, Iterator<Datum>
public class DataLoader extends Object implements Iterable<Datum>, Iterator<Datum>
S-expression reader.

Use readDatum() for checked I/O errors, or iterate and check lastIOException() afterwards. The loader itself is a one-shot iterator, and it depletes as soon as the underlying stream depletes or dies with an I/O error.

Caller is responsible for closing the supplied stream and to not share access across multiple threads, as this loader is not thread-safe. Most notably, writes to the symbol cache (if one is provided) is not synchronized, so it is possible that multiple newly encountered symbols are created. If this is a concern, use a fixed pool of symbols or provide a synchronized map like ConcurrentHashMap.

This loader assumes trusts its input, though some sane limits can be set using useDepthLimit(long) and useLengthLimit(long).

Example (by GPT): 


 try (Reader input = new java.io.StringReader("(name \"Ada\")")) {
     DataLoader loader = new DataLoader(input);
     Datum datum = loader.readDatum();
     java.util.List<Datum> array = Datum.asProperList(datum);
     assertEquals(Symbol.of("name"), array.get(0));
     assertEquals(Scalar.ofString("Ada"), array.get(1));
 }
Another example from me, if you wish to interpret as an alist: 

 try (Reader input = new java.io.StringReader("([name . \"Ada\"])")) {
     DataLoader loader = new DataLoader(input);
     Datum datum = loader.readDatum();
     java.util.Map<Datum,Datum> hash = Datum.asAlist(datum);
     assertEquals(Scalar.ofString("Ada"), hash.get(Symbol.of("name")));
     assertNull(hash.get(Symbol.of("NAME")));
 }

  • Method Details

    • useSymbolCache

      public final DataLoader useSymbolCache(Map<String,Symbol> cache)
      Use a map for symbol lookup upon construction. If null, remove the cache.

      Symbols not yet in the map are added to it, so the map grows as new vocabulary is read. If the map is read-only (such as one made by Map.of()), known symbols still resolve to the instances it holds, and unknown symbols are created without being remembered.

      The loader does not synchronize on the map. If it is shared between loaders running on different threads, it must be safe for concurrent use, such as a ConcurrentHashMap.

      Parameters:
      cache - map of symbols, optionally writable if the map is allowed to grow
      Returns:
      this
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • useDepthLimit

      public final DataLoader useDepthLimit(long depth)
      Limit how deeply lists may nest. A top-level atom has depth 0, and each enclosing list adds 1, so (a (b)) needs a limit of at least 2. A limit of 0 allows no lists at all. Exceeding the limit is a DataLoadingException.

      The loader recurses once per level, so a deep enough input can still exhaust the call stack below a high limit; set one when the input is not trusted. There is no limit by default.

      Parameters:
      depth - the most levels of nesting allowed
      Returns:
      this
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if depth is negative
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • unreadChar

      protected final void unreadChar(int v) throws IOException
      Pushes back a character. This also restores the cursor position to where it was before that character was read. Only the most recent call to readChar() can be undone this way, and only once; the position is not restored correctly if this is called twice in a row.
      Parameters:
      v - the character most recently returned by readChar()
      Throws:
      IOException - on I/O error
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • makeNumber

      protected Scalar makeNumber(String value)
      Hook called when a number-like token has been read. The loader only recognizes the shape of a number and does not convert it, so value is the token text as written. The cursor is already past the token, so a position reported from here points just after it.

    • makeList

      protected Cons makeList(Deque<Datum> q, Cons p)
      Hook called to create a non-empty list. The deque is constructed in FIFO order, meaning Deque.pop() or Deque.removeFirst() should be called to retrieve the last parsed datum. You are allowed (and even encouraged) to drain the deque!
      Parameters:
      q - list contents
      p - list trailer, containing exactly the last element and the list terminator
      Returns:
      a list
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • readDatum

      public Datum readDatum() throws IOException
      Reads and returns the next datum directly from the input. Caller must handle I/O side-effects.

      Caveat! This is a direct read and does not attempt to coordinate with the iterator interface. If hasNext() has already consumed a datum (i.e., returns true), you must drain it with next() as you will not get it again here.

      Returns:
      the next datum, or null on EOF
      Throws:
      IOException - on Reader.read(java.nio.CharBuffer) error
      DataLoadingException - on syntax error or an exceeded limit
